Okay, here's the current situation: My Fleshraker trigger is sitting pretty on the stack, above their Force of Will. Once that resolves, I get a spawn, and *then* my Fleshraker's ability triggers because the spawn is a colorless creature. I'm one step closer to figuring out the win here.

annotations.description: Playing a basic Island instead of Prismatic Vista or Tundra on turn 1 is slightly suboptimal. With Force of Will in hand (needing to exile a blue card), the player wants to preserve as many blue cards as possible and maximize mana flexibility. Playing Prismatic Vista first is generally correct because it can be cracked later to thin the deck and fetch whatever basic is needed, and it doesn't cost life until activated. More importantly, playing Tundra turn 1 would give access to both W and U mana, preserving flexibility for future turns. Playing a basic Island uses up a land drop that provides less flexibility than Tundra, and wastes a basic that could have been fetched later with Prismatic Vista.
annotations.actionTaken: Played a basic Island as the turn 1 land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play Prismatic Vista (or Tundra) as the turn 1 land, keeping basic Islands in the deck as fetch targets for later. Prismatic Vista turn 1 is standard because you can crack it on the opponent's end step if needed, and it preserves basics for future fetches.

annotations.description: Force of Will was spent (going card-negative) to counter a 1-mana utility artifact (Manifold Key) rather than saving it for the opponent's actual high-impact threats like Karn, the Great Creator or Glaring Fleshraker. Manifold Key is an enabler, not the payoff, and trading Force of Will + an exiled blue card for it is poor resource management.
annotations.actionTaken: Used Force of Will's alternative cost (paying 1 life and exiling a blue card) to counter Manifold Key
annotations.betterLine: Let Manifold Key resolve and save Force of Will for a more impactful spell like Karn, the Great Creator, Glaring Fleshraker, or another major threat. Develop the board by playing lands and Thundertrap Trainer to find answers.

annotations.description: Playing Ancient Tomb instead of Urza's Tower is suboptimal. With Planar Nexus on the battlefield (which counts as every nonbasic land type, including Urza's Mine and Urza's Power-Plant), playing Urza's Tower would give it the Tron bonus of 3 colorless mana instead of just 1. This means Urza's Tower + Planar Nexus produces 4 mana (3 from Tower + 1 from Nexus), which is enough to cast Karn, the Great Creator directly without needing Ancient Tomb's self-damage. With Ancient Tomb first, the player can still deploy their artifacts and potentially Karn, but they take 2 damage unnecessarily from Ancient Tomb when tapping it, and they miss out on the cleaner Tron-powered line. Playing Urza's Tower as the land drop, then tapping Tower for 3 + Nexus for 1 = 4 mana casts Karn cleanly with no life loss. Alternatively, Tower (3) + Nexus (1) could cast Grim Monolith (2) and still have mana left for Manifold Key (1) + Mox Opal (0), enabling even bigger plays.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Ancient Tomb as the land for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Urza's Tower to activate Tron with Planar Nexus. Tap Tower for 3 + Nexus for 1 = 4 mana, enough to cast Karn, the Great Creator directly without any life loss. Or use the mana to deploy Grim Monolith + Manifold Key + Mox Opal for an explosive setup.

annotations.description: Casting Glaring Fleshraker before deploying Mox Opal and Manifold Key is a sequencing error. By playing the cheaper artifacts first, Gem3P Valley could have achieved Metalcraft (Ancient Tomb + Planar Nexus + Mox Opal + Manifold Key = 3+ artifacts) to activate Mox Opal for mana, and then cast Fleshraker while also triggering Fleshraker's abilities off the colorless spells. More importantly, casting Fleshraker first means the artifacts played afterward will trigger Fleshraker's token-creation and damage abilities — but the issue is that Fleshraker costs 3 mana (Ancient Tomb for CC + Planar Nexus for C), using all available mana this turn. If Fleshraker had been cast after the 0-cost Mox Opal and 1-cost Manifold Key, those colorless spells would have triggered Fleshraker. The correct line is: cast Mox Opal (free), cast Manifold Key (1 mana from Planar Nexus), then cast Fleshraker (Ancient Tomb for CC + tap Mox Opal with Metalcraft for C). This way Fleshraker enters and then future colorless spells trigger it, plus you've deployed more of your hand. Actually, the key issue: by casting Fleshraker first using all mana, the other artifacts can still be cast afterward if mana is available. Let me re-check: Ancient Tomb gives CC, Planar Nexus gives C = 3 mana total for Fleshraker. After casting Fleshraker, no mana remains for Manifold Key. If instead: Mox Opal (0 mana), then need 1 for Manifold Key from Planar Nexus, then Fleshraker needs 2C+C = Ancient Tomb (CC) + Mox Opal (C with metalcraft from Tomb+Nexus+Opal+Key = 4 artifacts). This deploys 3 permanents instead of 1, gets Fleshraker triggers from Manifold Key (colorless spell → Spawn token + 1 damage), and sets up a much stronger board.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Glaring Fleshraker first, spending all available mana (Ancient Tomb + Planar Nexus), leaving no mana to deploy Mox Opal's metalcraft or Manifold Key this turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Mox Opal (free), then Manifold Key (1 mana from Planar Nexus), achieving Metalcraft, then cast Glaring Fleshraker (Ancient Tomb for CC + Mox Opal for C). This deploys 3 permanents, triggers Fleshraker once from the Manifold Key cast (creating a Spawn + dealing 1 damage), and leaves a much stronger board state.

annotations.description: Fetching Mountain instead of Island is suboptimal. The player's hand contains Force of Will, Thundertrap Trainer, and an Island. Thundertrap Trainer costs 1U, and Force of Will's alternative cost requires exiling a blue card. The player already has a Tundra (which produces U or W) and is fetching off Prismatic Vista. Getting another Island provides more consistent blue mana access for casting Force of Will normally (3UU) if needed later, and there are no red cards in hand or any apparent reason to need Mountain. While Tundra already covers white mana, an extra Island is strictly better than Mountain given the hand and deck composition appears to be primarily blue-based.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched Mountain from library with Prismatic Vista
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Island to have more consistent blue mana for Force of Will and Thundertrap Trainer, since there are no red spells in hand or apparent reason to need red mana

annotations.description: With Force of Will already in hand and another Force of Will available from Thundertrap Trainer's trigger, the player chose Ponder over the second Force of Will. The opponent has Glaring Fleshraker on board generating tokens and pinging, plus Karn, the Great Creator is a likely threat from a Tron/artifact deck. Having a second Force of Will would provide stronger countermagic protection (one to cast, one to pitch to the other, or pitch the hand copy to the revealed one). Ponder is a cantrip that helps find answers but doesn't guarantee finding anything better than what Force of Will already provides. However, Ponder does help dig for specific answers and the player already has one Force of Will, so this is debatable.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Ponder from Thundertrap Trainer's trigger over Force of Will
annotations.betterLine: Take Force of Will to have two copies — enabling the alternate cost (exile one blue card + 1 life) while still having countermagic, giving stronger protection against the opponent's powerful spells like Karn

annotations.description: Casting Karn before Manifold Key misses value. With Urza's Tower producing 3 mana (thanks to Planar Nexus providing Mine/Power-Plant types) plus 2 Spawn sacrifices = 5 mana total, they could cast Manifold Key first ({1}), triggering Glaring Fleshraker to create a Spawn token and deal 1 damage, then still have 4 mana left (2 from Tower + 2 Spawn sacs) for Karn. This would net an extra 1 damage to opponent, an extra Spawn token, and Manifold Key on the battlefield.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Karn, the Great Creator first without playing Manifold Key beforehand.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Manifold Key first (triggering Fleshraker for a Spawn + 1 damage), then cast Karn, the Great Creator with remaining mana. This nets an extra damage, extra Spawn token, and gets Manifold Key onto the battlefield.

annotations.description: Liquimetal Coating + Karn's +1 is a land destruction combo, but the opponent is at 14 life with 3 Eldrazi Spawn tokens, Glaring Fleshraker, and Karn already on board. The opponent has no cards in hand and all lands tapped, so they're in a weak position. Mystic Forge would enable much more explosive turns by casting artifacts off the top of the library, chaining into more Spawn tokens and Fleshraker triggers for damage, potentially closing the game quickly. Liquimetal Coating is a slow 2-card combo that destroys one land per turn and doesn't advance the board or deal damage. With Grim Monolith in the graveyard (recoverable later) and the ability to chain artifacts, Mystic Forge seems significantly stronger for pressing the advantage.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched Liquimetal Coating from sideboard with Karn's -2 ability
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Mystic Forge to enable casting artifacts off the top of the library, generating more Eldrazi Spawn tokens via Glaring Fleshraker and dealing significant damage to close the game faster. Alternatively, Portable Hole could exile a problematic permanent if needed for immediate impact.

annotations.description: The player's stated goal is to set up the Liquimetal Coating + Karn land destruction engine. Casting Manifold Key first (1 mana) before Liquimetal Coating (2 mana) is fine for sequencing since both can be cast this turn, but the reasoning is slightly confused. More importantly, casting Manifold Key first triggers Glaring Fleshraker to create a Spawn token, which enables Metalcraft for Mox Opal (Mox Opal + Manifold Key + Liquimetal Coating = 3 artifacts once Coating is cast). However, the player could have achieved the same result by casting Liquimetal Coating first (also triggers Fleshraker, also gets to 3 artifacts with Mox Opal + Coating + then Manifold Key). The sequencing is essentially equivalent for mana purposes. The real question is whether Mystic Forge should have been prioritized over Manifold Key, since Mystic Forge provides much more card advantage and the Manifold Key doesn't have an immediate high-value untap target. But given the player wants to establish the Coating+Karn lock and has enough mana for both Manifold Key and Coating this turn, this is a reasonable line. The play is acceptable.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Manifold Key before Liquimetal Coating
annotations.betterLine: Cast Liquimetal Coating first to immediately enable the Karn +1 land destruction combo, then cast Manifold Key with remaining mana. The order doesn't matter much here since both will be cast, but leading with the more impactful piece is slightly better in case the opponent has interaction.

annotations.description: By activating Karn +1 first (which is free), they could still cast Mystic Forge afterward, but the activation is a loyalty ability usable once per turn. The real issue is sequencing - they should cast Mystic Forge first using Urza's Tower (1) + Mox Opal (1) + 2 Spawn sacrifices (2) = 4 mana, triggering Glaring Fleshraker for 1 damage and a Spawn token, THEN activate Karn +1 on Tundra. Both plays are available this turn, and casting Mystic Forge first gets them the engine piece plus an extra point of damage and token.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Karn +1 first targeting opponent's Tundra (made artifact by Liquimetal Coating) to destroy it.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Mystic Forge first (using Urza's Tower + Mox Opal + 2 Spawn sacrifices for 4 mana), getting Fleshraker trigger (1 damage + Spawn token), then activate Karn +1 on Tundra to destroy it. Gets both plays plus extra value.

annotations.description: With 14 sideboard artifacts available via Karn's -2 and plenty of mana (Urza's Tower producing 3 mana with Planar Nexus completing Tron, plus Spawn sacrifices and Mox Opal), using Karn's +1 to animate an artifact is likely weaker than using -2 to tutor a powerful artifact from the sideboard. The +1 only creates a small attacker, while -2 could fetch a game-ending threat or key utility artifact, especially since Gem3P Valley also has Mystic Forge in hand ready to deploy.
annotations.actionTaken: Used Karn's +1 to animate a noncreature artifact
annotations.betterLine: Use Karn's -2 to fetch a powerful artifact from the sideboard (e.g., a threat or combo piece), then deploy Mystic Forge with remaining mana to generate card advantage

annotations.description: Passed the turn with 7+ mana available (Urza's Tower with Tron online via Planar Nexus = 3, Mox Opal = 1, 3 Eldrazi Spawn = 3) and Mystic Forge in hand castable for 4. Mystic Forge is a powerful card advantage engine that would be very strong here. The reasoning described wanting to use Manifold Key to untap Liquimetal Coating to lock opponent's Mountain, but then chose to pass without doing anything.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any spells or activating any abilities.
annotations.betterLine: At minimum, cast Mystic Forge for 4 mana (Tower + Opal or Spawn tokens). Could also first activate Manifold Key (1 + tap) to untap Liquimetal Coating, use Coating to make opponent's Mountain an artifact (locked by Karn), then cast Mystic Forge with remaining mana.

annotations.description: Chose to draw 2 cards with Flame of Anor instead of killing Glaring Fleshraker, which is the key engine generating Spawn tokens and dealing incremental damage. While drawing cards can find answers, Fleshraker alive means each colorless spell the opponent casts next turn creates more tokens and deals more damage, accelerating the clock.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Flame of Anor choosing mode 1 (draw two cards) targeting self
annotations.betterLine: Cast Flame of Anor choosing mode 3 (deal 5 damage to target creature) targeting Glaring Fleshraker to shut down the token/damage engine and buy time to stabilize

annotations.description: Gem3P Valley used Karn's +1 to animate the opponent's Mountain (which was already an artifact due to Liquimetal Coating). As a 0-mana-value permanent, it becomes a 0/0 creature and dies to state-based actions, destroying the opponent's land. While this is a legitimate line to deny a mana source, the opponent is already at 9 life with 5 Eldrazi Spawn tokens and a Glaring Fleshraker on board. Animating Manifold Key (MV 1, becomes a 1/1 artifact creature) would have given an additional attacker and also enabled the +1/+1 counter from Tezzeret's 0 ability on future turns. Alternatively, the opponent has only 4 lands and is nearly dead - removing one land is fine but the game might have been better served by building the board for a lethal attack this turn or next. With 5 Spawn tokens, Glaring Fleshraker (2/2), and potentially a 1/1 Manifold Key creature, that's potentially more damage. However, denying the Mountain removes the opponent's only red source and their ability to cast removal like Flame of Anor, so this is defensible. It's close enough to be questionable rather than clearly wrong.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted opponent's Mountain with Karn's +1 to turn it into a 0/0 artifact creature, destroying it via state-based actions.
annotations.betterLine: Could have targeted own Manifold Key to create a 1/1 artifact creature for additional board presence and attack potential, since the opponent is at 9 life with significant board advantage already established. The opponent's red source removal is valuable though, making this debatable.

annotations.description: By casting Mystic Forge before Tezzeret, Cruel Captain, Gem3P missed 2 loyalty counters on Tezzeret. If Tezzeret were on the battlefield first, it would gain a loyalty counter when Mystic Forge enters (artifact entering) and another when the Eldrazi Spawn token enters from Fleshraker's trigger. This is a sequencing error that costs meaningful planeswalker value.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Mystic Forge first, then planned to cast Tezzeret afterward
annotations.betterLine: Cast Tezzeret, Cruel Captain first (3 mana: Ancient Tomb + 1 land), then cast Mystic Forge (4 mana: remaining land + Opal + 2 Spawns). Tezzeret would have entered at 4 loyalty and gained +2 from Mystic Forge and its Spawn token entering, reaching 6 loyalty.

annotations.description: Exiled Kozilek's Command off the top with Mystic Forge rather than potentially casting it. With Mox Opal, Manifold Key, and 6 Eldrazi Spawn tokens available for mana, there may have been enough resources to cast Kozilek's Command from the top of the library for a meaningful X value, especially since each colorless spell cast would trigger Glaring Fleshraker for additional damage against an opponent at 8 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Mystic Forge to exile Kozilek's Command from the top of the library, paying 1 life.
annotations.betterLine: Check if Kozilek's Command could be cast from the top using Spawn tokens and Mox Opal mana. Even a modest X value would trigger Fleshraker and potentially deal significant damage or generate value. If truly uncastable due to mana constraints, the exile is fine.

annotations.description: With the opponent at 8 life and Gem3P Valley having Glaring Fleshraker plus 6 Eldrazi Spawn tokens on board, Karn the Great Creator could have been more impactful this turn. Karn's -2 can fetch an artifact from the sideboard (they have 14 sideboard cards), potentially grabbing a key combo piece or win condition. Karn also shuts down the opponent's artifact activated abilities (though the opponent has no artifacts currently). More importantly, Karn at 5 loyalty is a more resilient threat than Tezzeret at 4 loyalty. However, Tezzeret's 0 ability to untap artifacts provides immediate value with Mystic Forge (which is tapped) and Manifold Key, potentially enabling further combo turns. Tezzeret also gains loyalty from artifact ETBs, synergizing with the Spawn token generation. The choice between the two is genuinely close and depends on what's in the sideboard, but casting Karn first to fetch a powerful artifact with -2 (like a Grim Monolith from exile or another combo piece from sideboard) before spending mana on Tezzeret seems potentially stronger, as it converts immediately into a card while still leaving Karn at 3 loyalty.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Tezzeret, Cruel Captain for 3 mana
annotations.betterLine: Cast Karn, the Great Creator for 4 mana (sacrificing a Spawn token for the extra mana), then use -2 to fetch a key artifact from the sideboard or reclaim Kozilek's Command/Grim Monolith from exile, providing immediate card advantage and potentially enabling a lethal line

annotations.description: Failed to use Tezzeret, Cruel Captain's 0 ability before combat to put a +1/+1 counter on an Eldrazi Spawn token (making it a 1/2 artifact creature), which would have allowed attacking for 3 total damage instead of 2. With the opponent at 7 life, every point of damage matters. Planeswalkers can activate abilities the turn they enter.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Glaring Fleshraker for 2 damage, leaving Tezzeret's 0 ability unused before combat.
annotations.betterLine: Use Tezzeret's 0 ability to put a +1/+1 counter on a non-summoning-sick Eldrazi Spawn token, then attack with both Glaring Fleshraker and the pumped Spawn for 3 total damage.

annotations.description: At 5 life facing a board with Glaring Fleshraker, 7 Eldrazi Spawn tokens (5 non-summoning-sick), Karn, Tezzeret, and multiple artifacts, the player is in a dire position. Loch Mare is a 1/2 body (4/5 with three -1/-1 counters) that could block and potentially buy time, plus its counter-removal abilities could draw cards. Casting Ponder first to look for better answers is reasonable sequencing (cast cantrip before committing to a creature), but given the opponent's overwhelming board and the player being at 5 life, there's an argument that deploying the blocker immediately is more important — especially since Ponder costs the same U mana that could be held for Stern Scolding. However, Ponder-first is standard cantrip sequencing to find the best possible line, so this is debatable rather than clearly wrong.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Ponder before deploying Loch Mare as a potential blocker
annotations.betterLine: This is debatable — Ponder first is standard sequencing to see more cards, but deploying Loch Mare as a blocker while holding up Stern Scolding mana might have been preferable given the lethal-on-board pressure

annotations.description: Opponent is at 2 life with Loch Mare tapped. Gem3P Valley already has Glaring Fleshraker (2/2) on board that can attack for exactly lethal this turn. Casting a second Fleshraker before combat using Ancient Tomb costs 2 unnecessary life (going from 7 to 5) and wastes a card from hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Glaring Fleshraker using Ancient Tomb (taking 2 damage) before going to combat.
annotations.betterLine: Go directly to combat and attack with the existing 2/2 Glaring Fleshraker for exactly lethal against the 2-life opponent with no untapped blockers.
